per_scenario.outcome_reason: root cause R3 failed; false top candidate=checkout
per_scenario.detail: payment is a LEAF node in the oracle PAG. It has no outgoing directed edges to any diverging service. R3 requires a causal path to at least one other diverging service — payment has none. checkout (its caller) satisfies R3 because it can reach payment downstream. This is an inverted-graph attribution: the oracle PAG uses call-graph direction (caller->callee), so payment appears as a SINK, not a SOURCE.

redis_cart is detected (R1 pass, top_candidate=redis_cart) but RIFT outputs confidence=NONE because R3 fails — cart does not appear in the oracle PAG variables (redis_cart->cart edge exists, cart anomaly not independently detected as diverging). The system correctly finds the root cause service but cannot emit CANDIDATE/DEFINITIVE because R3 evidence chain is incomplete. Counted as incorrect because top_confidence=NONE is excluded from root_cause_found check.

per_scenario.detail: Same leaf-node R3 failure as SD_01. product_catalog is a SINK in the oracle PAG (recommendation->product_catalog direction). R3 requires product_catalog to have a downstream diverging service — it has none. recommendation satisfies R3 because it can reach product_catalog. This is structurally identical to the SD_01 failure mode.

per_scenario.note: All 24 confounded scenarios (CF_00 through CF_23) classified as B_correct_abstention. Each has: confounded=True, assumption_warnings present (BIDIRECTED edge detected), identifiability_state=NOT_IDENTIFIABLE. V2=100% PASS.

leaf_node_r3_failure.root_mechanism: Root-cause service is a SINK (leaf node) in the oracle PAG. R3 requires the candidate to have a directed path to at least one other diverging service. Leaf nodes have no outgoing edges in the call-graph-derived PAG, so R3 always fails. The intermediate caller (checkout, recommendation, checkout) satisfies R3 and becomes the false top candidate.

confidence_none_r3_failure.root_mechanism: redis_cart->cart path exists in oracle PAG. redis_cart correctly identified (R1+R2 pass, top_candidate=redis_cart) but cart does not independently cross the R1 detection threshold in the incident window. R3 requires a DIVERGING downstream service; cart does not diverge strongly enough. Confidence stays NONE. Root cause is nominally top but excluded from V1 count because confidence!=CANDIDATE.

structural_finding: All 6 non-confounded failures trace to a single root cause: R3 (causal relevance) fails when the true root-cause service is a LEAF NODE in the oracle PAG. The oracle PAG is derived from CALL_GRAPH direction (caller->callee), meaning callee/sink services (payment, product_catalog, redis_cart) cannot satisfy R3. This is a structural mismatch between R3's design assumption (root cause has downstream effects in the graph) and the RIFT topology encoding (faults that propagate UP from called services to callers).
analysis_notes: The 50% raw V1 decomposes as: 6/12 correct (50%) = 6 correct + 4 H_intervention_failure + 2 C_incorrect_attribution.
Of the 6 failures: 4 are H_intervention_failure (R3 leaf-node) and 2 are C_incorrect_attribution (R3+confidence=NONE).
All 24 confounded scenarios produce B_correct_abstention — V2=100%. This means 30/36 scenarios (83.3%) have CORRECT behavior.
The failing 6 are all non-confounded and all fail due to the same structural issue: R3 cannot be satisfied by leaf-node (sink) services in the oracle call-graph PAG.
Conditional Precision@1 (excluding NOT_IDENTIFIABLE confounded) = 6/10 = 60%. Note: identifiable non-confounded = 10 (leaf nodes RC_01, RC_02 are technically identifiable but R3-limited).

FAR=33.3% (4 of 12): four scenarios produce a false top candidate (checkout or recommendation) instead of the true root cause (payment or product_catalog). These are NOT random errors — they are systematic: caller is always ranked above callee.

The oracle PAG uses only DIRECTED edges from the call graph. In production with FCI-estimated PAG, edge directionality would be uncertain (partially directed / circle marks), which could HELP or HURT: FCI might orient some edges in the opposite direction relative to the call graph, potentially allowing leaf-node services to satisfy R3 in some cases.
Coverage = 100%: RIFT produces output for every scenario. Abstention rate = 0% on non-confounded (expected — R1 always fires for these scenarios).
The non-identifiability rate (66.7%) is almost entirely due to the 24 confounded scenarios, where BIDIRECTED edges correctly trigger NOT_IDENTIFIABLE. This is correct behavior.
caveat: Oracle PAG used. V1=50% is upper-bound estimate. FCI-estimated PAG may produce different (potentially better or worse) results depending on edge orientation recovery.
